script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is form-only. Base flow is blitz-shaped, not a shootout: TB blitzes 46% and Love's EPA/dropback is -0.28 on 58 blitzed dropbacks versus +0.19 unblitzed, so GB's deep air (Golden 416 air yards, Watson 304) gets capped and the ball comes out shorter. TB's run defense (3.30 YPC, only 6 runs of 10+) stalls a GB committee already inefficient (Lloyd 23/68, 2.96 YPC). The usable path is TB's: Irving (40 carries, 180 yards, 4.5 YPC) into GB's soft run front (4.34 YPC, 8 runs of 10+), with Mayfield inefficient either way (-0.26 vs blitz, -0.25 clean) so TB can feed Irving on the ground and Otton in the middle (GB middle 8.77 YPA) without needing a track meet.
script.flip1: Love handles the blitz the way he does unblitzed (+0.19 EPA). Golden (84.3 rec yds/g) and Watson (94.7) clear, GB plays from in front, and TB abandons the run — Irving's rush line dies while Otton/Egbuka/Godwin targets rise.
script.flip2: Low-event slog: the 46% blitz plus GB allowing only 5 passes of 20+ on 98 attempts drags everything down. Irving still gets carries, but even Otton's middle targets come in light if Mayfield's negative EPA shows up as few completions rather than just inefficient ones.

injury_fallout: No injury report, practice trend, or inactives in the pack, so no next-man-up can be assigned and late-scratch risk is unpriced. Carry log only: GB is a committee (Lloyd 23/68, K.Johnson 12/38, Brooks 11/40, Love 2/0); TB is Irving's backfield (Irving 40/180, Mayfield 10/66, Gainwell 10/21, Godwin 2/15). Kaleb Johnson's 31.5 rush line versus 12.7 yds/g, and Jalon Daniels 33.5 with zero listed carries, imply role news this pack does not contain — those markets are unused.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location splits are the proxy. TB: middle 9.47 YPA on 17 att versus left 6.57 (44 att) and right 6.36 (33 att) — middle open, perimeter sound. GB: middle 8.77 on 13 att, left 7.66 (35), right 6.63 (41) — same shape, right side is GB's best.
matchup.pressure: TB blitz rate 46% is the slate signal; Love EPA -0.28 vs blitz (n=58) vs +0.19 clean, so pressure that looks like this blitz profile kills GB deep yards and should funnel shorter throws. GB blitzes only 35%, and Mayfield is equally poor vs blitz (-0.26, n=43) and clean (-0.25), so GB pressure is not a differentiator.
matchup.bleeds: TB bleeds the middle and has been stingy vs the run (3.30 YPC, 6 runs of 10+) while allowing 8 explosives on 100 pass attempts. GB bleeds the run (4.34 YPC, 8 runs of 10+) and the middle, but has limited explosives (5/98).
matchup.overlap: Otton (17 targets, 120 yards, 138 air, ~8.1 aDOT) is the TB pass option that actually attacks GB's middle hole. Irving's 13.3 carries/game at 4.5 YPC attacks GB's run bleed. Golden (30 tgt, 13.9 aDOT) and Watson (29 tgt, 10.5 aDOT) attack deep/perimeter, which is not TB's bleed (perimeter YPA 6.4-6.6) and runs into the 46% blitz — overlap fails, so they are not legs.

form: Avoiding season averages; L3 role only, and the pack has no similar-defense splits. GB: Golden 30/253/416 and Watson 29/284/304 are the alphas; Kraft 17/106/128 is the real TE (35.3 yds/g, under a 40.5 line); Moore 11/37, Reed 8/24, Smith 6/66 (efficient, tiny sample), Lloyd 6/13 receiving. Lloyd leads rushes but at 2.96 YPC; Johnson and Brooks are live committee pieces, not ghosts. TB: Irving 40/180 rush plus 15/61 receiving on -33 air (checkdown role, ~20 rec yds/g). Egbuka 20/141/250 (~47 yds/g, 12.5 aDOT). Otton 17/120/138 (~40 yds/g). Hurst 13/103/250 and Tez Johnson 7/57/210 are explosive-air profiles against a GB defense that has allowed only 5 passes of 20+ — treat as fluky, not edges. Godwin 11/111/52 is short and efficient (10.1 yards/target) and can regress. Gainwell 10/21 rush and 10/22 receiving is the change-of-pace, not the engine.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Otton is already at 40 receiving yards a game on 17 targets, and Green Bay's only soft passing zone is the middle (8.77 YPA), which is where this tight end lives; 25.5 sits about 15 yards under that role.
edge_players.must_be_true: Otton plays his normal route share (about 5-6 targets), Mayfield still throws middle, and he is active — no injury note exists in the pack to confirm that.
edge_players.kills_it: TB goes run-extreme and Otton sees two targets, or GB takes the middle away and his looks move to the right side where GB allows only 6.63 YPA.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Irving is the only back with a real carry share (40 carries, 60 rush yards a game, 4.5 YPC) and he runs into the defense allowing 4.34 YPC and 8 runs of 10+, so 55.5 is a small step under both the role and the matchup. Script-dependent: it needs TB not to be trailing big.
edge_players.must_be_true: He keeps roughly 13 carries, stays active, and the game stays close enough that TB does not abandon the run. Spread is not in the pack, so that script is inferred, not priced.
edge_players.kills_it: Flip 1: GB hits the deep shots, TB trails, and Irving finishes something like 11 carries at a stuffed YPC (10 at 4.0 is 40, under 55.5). A snap limit or Mayfield/Gainwell stealing early-down work does the same.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so this check is L3 role versus the listed price only. Otton 40.0 vs 25.5 and Irving 60.0 vs 55.5 both sit on the over side of the rung — agree, and size Otton larger because the cushion is ~14.5 yards versus ~4.5. Dropped leans, not flagged: a Golden under 57.5 or Watson under 68 is the blitz read (Love -0.28 EPA vs a 46% blitz), but L3 yards (84.3 and 94.7) disagree hard, and without a pressure rate those are leans, so the lean-disagree rule cuts them rather than flagging a strong read. Johnson under 31.5 and Daniels 33.5 were not used because the lines imply roles the carry log does not show. No model probability is available to treat as a suspicious 70%+.

market_rung_price: Cade Otton recyds over 25.5 -111 (primary, middle-field volume). Bucky Irving rushyds over 55.5 -115.5 (smaller, script-dependent run leg). Irving rush+rec over 72 would add cushion (L3 combined ~80) but that price is not saved (+nan), so the priced rush rung is the one used. No receptions, passing yards, or TD markets.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Otton: Mayfield's negative EPA showed up as a short, run-heavy day; Egbuka (20 L3 targets) and Godwin took the intermediate looks and Otton finished 3-18. The 8.77 middle YPA was only 13 attempts, and GB sat a body in the hook all night. Irving: GB keyed the bellcow, held him near 3.1 YPC, and once Love wasn't blitzed at the 46% season rate the deep shots hit, TB trailed, and Irving had 11 carries for 44. The 4.5-yard cushion was noise around a line the market had right, and Mayfield's 10 designed runs (66 yards) stole the easy ones. If that counter-case is how you see it, the Irving lean is the leg to pass, not Otton.
slip_story: One story: TB's balanced control script. Irving rush over is the run leg into GB's leaky front; Otton rec over is the middle pass leg in the same offense. They win together if TB stays competitive and uses both. Do not add Golden or Watson overs — those need the Love-beats-blitz flip, the opposite script. No TDs, one market per player, two legs.
